## Q. Interval-arithmetic cover of eps (python-flint balls; K <= 3, n = 1)

For each target the certificate S(eps) was verified in ball arithmetic on a chain of balls covering **every real eps in [10^-24, 10^top]** (top = the highest exponent from which the chain closes; "float eps_0" is the half-decade grid value of theory_t1.md).  Candidate D_j from the floating-point certificate (x1.1 ... x4), then every ingredient re-evaluated with outward-rounded balls (see theory_t1b_rigorous.py).  Inputs taken as exact floating-point numbers: the limit object's data (critical points, entry times, duals at the breakpoints, rates, margins, the entrant/feature assignment); the final comparisons use the float upper end of a ball; the hypotheses r > d_0, the block critical point in the relaxation set D-hat and theta < v_# are checked against ball constants with floating-point limit data (asserted in the current `verify`; see theory_t1b_reverify.md for the rerun of these covers with the amended verifier).  Statement: S(eps) evaluated in interval arithmetic, with floating-point limit-object data, for every real eps in the ball.

8 of 10 targets: the certificate holds, in ball arithmetic, for every real eps in [10^-24, 10^top] (the chain of balls above; top < float eps_0 when the interval tests fail close to the float threshold).  For the others the chain stopped (interval test failed at the smallest ball width tried, 1/512 decade, or the time budget of 240 s per attempt ran out): it covers every real eps in [10^lowest, 10^top] only.  These stops are outcomes of the search budget and of the ball width (the window-start gating of the drift terms becomes undecided on wide balls), not evidence that S fails there (referee round T1b, finding 4).

## U. The eps-uniform envelope of the dormant coefficient (Lemma 12.4)

This is the envelope version of the dormant-coefficient bound: it bounds B_eps(s) by an eps-uniform envelope; it does not by itself make the exact mass and drift monotone in eps, and the layer constants remain unsigned.  Valid for lambda >= 25, i.e. eps <~ 0.03 (and eps < 2 v_s).

B_eps(s) <= 4/(G gamma^2 m) (1 - (20/s)^2)^-1 s^-3 for all eps and s >= 25 (Lemma 2.2 + Adamovic-Mitrinovic: min over a 2e5-point grid of (sin t)^3/(t^3 cos t) on (0, pi/2) = 1.000000 >= 1).
